Interface RainbowGum

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable, LogEventLogger
public sealed interface RainbowGum extends AutoCloseable, LogEventLogger
The main entry point and configuration of RainbowGum logging.

RainbowGum logging loads configuration through the service loader. While you can manually set RainbowGum using set(Supplier) it is better to register implementations through the ServiceLoader so that RainbowGum will load prior to any external logging.

To register a custom RainbowGum: 


class RainbowGumProviderExample implements RainbowGumProvider {

	@Override
	public Optional<RainbowGum> provide(LogConfig config) {

		Integer bufferSize = config.properties() //
			.forKey("logging.custom.async.bufferSize")
			.ofInt()
			.or(1024)
			.validateNow(RainbowGumProviderExample.class);

		LogProvider<LogOutput> output = (name, cfg) -> cfg.properties()
			.forKey("logging.custom.output")
			.ofProvider(LogOutput::of)
			.or(LogOutput.ofStandardOut())
			.validateNow(RainbowGumProviderExample.class)
			.provide(name, cfg);

		var gum = RainbowGum.builder() //
			.route(r -> {
				r.publisher(PublisherFactory //
					.async() //
					.bufferSize(bufferSize) //
					.build());
				r.appender("console", a -> {
					a.output(output);
				});
				r.level(Level.INFO);
			})
			.build();

		return Optional.of(gum);
	}

}

Initialization order - most of the actual work happens in LogConfig.Builder.build(), LogRouter.Router.Builder, and LogAppenderRegistry; this is the exact sequence for anyone debugging a configuration or writing a RainbowGumServiceProvider.RainbowGumProvider:

  1. LogConfig.Builder.build() builds the shared LogConfig:
    1. Resolve the ServiceRegistry (default: a new empty one) and LogProperties - manually added RainbowGumServiceProvider.PropertiesProviders, else (if a ServiceLoader was supplied) SPI-discovered ones, with system properties always layered in as a final fallback.
    2. Build LogAlerts and LogMetrics from properties.
    3. Build the global level resolver (logging.level.* and logging.group.*, plus anything added directly on the builder).
    4. Construct the LogConfig itself - this is also where a few process-wide flags get latched (config change support, the appender lock, and thread-local-disabled globals) and the default output/encoder/publisher registries are created.
    5. Run every RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator (manually added, then SPI-discovered), highest priority first. A configurator returning false is retried in a later pass (see RainbowGumServiceProvider.PASSES) - useful if it depends on another configurator running first.
    6. Start LogAlerts - deliberately last, so a configurator's own alert listener is already registered before alerts decides whether an unobserved error should refuse startup.
  2. RainbowGum.Builder.build() builds each named LogRouter.Router (a single route named "default", unless logging.routes names several) via LogRouter.Router.Builder's own (package-private) build():
    1. Resolve route flags (logging.route.<name>.flags).
    2. Build a route-scoped level resolver: anything configured directly on the route builder, layered over logging.route.<name>.level.*, falling back to the global level resolver from step 1 (skipped entirely if the route flag IGNORE_GLOBAL_LEVEL_RESOLVER is set) - and finally to INFO if nothing at all resolves a level.
    3. Resolve appenders - only if none were added programmatically on the route builder (that check is all-or-nothing: adding even one appender in code skips property-based resolution entirely). See Appender resolution below.
    4. Resolve the publisher - logging.route.<name>.publisher, falling back to a synchronous publisher if unset.
    5. Hand the resolved appenders to the publisher and register the publisher in the ServiceRegistry.
  3. start() starts the root router, which starts each route's publisher, which starts each of its appenders, which starts its output (e.g. opening a file).
Appender resolution - the part most often mistaken for a bug, since no appenders are ever added programmatically in the common case:
  1. logging.route.<name>.appenders names the route's appenders; for the "default" route only, a missing value falls back to the unprefixed logging.appenders.
  2. If that is still missing: for the default route only, the list defaults to [file, console] if logging.file.name (or Spring Boot's convention) is set, otherwise just [console]. A non-default route with no appenders configured anywhere is a startup failure, not a silent no-op.
  3. Each named appender then resolves independently. file and console are the two built-in special cases, each with its own output property/fallback (logging.file.name then logging.appender.file.output for file; logging.appender.console.output falling back to standard-out for console). Any other name is fully generic: logging.appender.<name>.output/.encoder/.flags/ .type, with the output's own URI scheme choosing which registered LogOutput.OutputProvider builds it.
  4. An output can supply its own encoder by implementing LogOutput.ProvidesEncoder (rare, e.g. some structured outputs): with LogOutput.ProvidesEncoder.Policy.MANDATORY that encoder is used as-is and the .encoder property is never consulted (configuring one anyway is a startup failure); with LogOutput.ProvidesEncoder.Policy.DEFAULT it is only a fallback and the .encoder property, if set, still wins. An output that does not implement LogOutput.ProvidesEncoder at all is unaffected - the .encoder property (or the registry's default for the output's type) always applies.

  • Method Details

    • of

      static RainbowGum of()
      Gets the currently statically bound RainbowGum and will try to load and find one if there is none currently bound. This is a blocking operation as in locks are used and will block indefinitely till a gum has loaded. If that is not desired see getOrNull().
      Returns:
      current RainbowGum or new loaded one.

    • getOrNull

      static @Nullable RainbowGum getOrNull()
      Gets the currently statically bound RainbowGum or null if none are finished binding. Unlike of() this will never load or start an instance but rather just gets the currently bound one. It will also never block and does not wait if one is currently being loaded.
      Returns:
      current RainbowGum or null

    • onGlobalChange

      static void onGlobalChange(Consumer<RainbowGum> consumer)
      Subscribes to notification of a new RainbowGum becoming the globally bound one (see set(Supplier), set(RainbowGum), RainbowGum.Builder.set()). This is primarily for components like SLF4J's logger factory that are themselves bootstrapped once (often before "the real" RainbowGum has loaded, e.g. a framework's own pre-boot sequence) and otherwise have no way of finding out that a different RainbowGum has since replaced the one they captured.

      Only a weak reference to consumer is retained, so subscribing does not by itself keep the consumer (or whatever it is attached to) reachable - the caller is responsible for keeping a strong reference to consumer for as long as it needs to keep receiving notifications, otherwise it may silently stop being called once garbage collected.

      Parameters:
      consumer - called with the newly bound global RainbowGum. Never called while any RainbowGum internal lock is held.
